questions.competency: VII.B — Foundational Operations Concepts, Resource Protection, and Incident Management
questions.skill: Applying least privilege when provisioning access for a new hire in a sensitive role
questions.performanceIndicator: Scope initial access to the specific duties of a new position rather than a broad role template
questions.scenarioContext: An investment bank's identity team is provisioning system access for a newly hired trade settlement analyst. The standard onboarding template for the settlement department includes access to several systems the new analyst's specific duties will not require.
questions.prompt: What should the identity team do?

choices.A: Grant the full departmental template so the analyst never has to request additional access later
choices.B: Provision only the access required for the analyst's specific assigned duties, adding more only if justified later
choices.C: Delay provisioning any access until the analyst has worked in the role for several months
choices.D: Copy the exact access profile of the most senior analyst on the team

questions.explanation: Least privilege calls for provisioning only the access the new analyst's actual duties require, with additional access added later if a specific, justified need arises. Granting the full template regardless of need creates unnecessary exposure. Withholding all access delays legitimate work, and copying a senior analyst's profile typically grants far more access than a new hire's duties warrant.

questions.competency: VII.B — Foundational Operations Concepts, Resource Protection, and Incident Management
questions.skill: Managing planned decommissioning of end-of-life assets still processing production data
questions.performanceIndicator: Apply asset lifecycle controls when retiring equipment that remains in active use
questions.scenarioContext: A grocery retail chain's asset inventory shows that several point-of-sale servers have reached the end of their supported life and are scheduled for replacement next quarter. The servers currently continue to process daily transaction data.
questions.prompt: What should the asset management process require before the servers are removed from service?

choices.A: Confirm data migration or backup, verify successor systems are ready, and schedule sanitization or destruction of the retired hardware
choices.B: Power off the servers immediately once the replacement date arrives, regardless of data status
choices.C: Leave the retired servers connected as an informal backup with no further tracking
choices.D: Transfer the servers to another department without updating asset or data-handling records

questions.explanation: A controlled decommissioning process confirms that data has been migrated or preserved, that replacement systems are ready to take over processing, and that retired hardware is sanitized or destroyed according to its data sensitivity. Powering off servers without confirming data status risks loss of unprocessed transactions. Leaving retired systems connected without tracking, or transferring them without updated records, both undermine asset accountability.

questions.competency: VII.B — Foundational Operations Concepts, Resource Protection, and Incident Management
questions.skill: Triaging and prioritizing multiple simultaneous security alerts
questions.performanceIndicator: Apply risk-based criteria to sequence incident response when several alerts arrive at once
questions.scenarioContext: A telecommunications carrier's security operations center receives three alerts within minutes of each other: an employee-reported phishing email, indicators of active data exfiltration from a customer billing server, and a spike in failed logins on a test system that was decommissioned months ago.
questions.prompt: Which THREE practices should the team apply when triaging these alerts? Select 3 of the 5 options below.

choices.A: Rank the alerts using business impact, asset criticality, and evidence of active compromise
choices.B: Investigate each alert strictly in the order it arrived, regardless of apparent severity
choices.C: Escalate the exfiltration indicator immediately while queuing the lower-risk items for scheduled review
choices.D: Close alerts that lack an obvious technical indicator without recording the reasoning
choices.E: Document the triage decisions and supporting rationale for later review

questions.explanation: Risk-based ranking, immediate escalation of the highest-impact indicator, and documented triage decisions together support a defensible and effective response when multiple alerts compete for attention. Strict arrival-order handling could delay response to the active exfiltration. Closing alerts without recorded justification removes the ability to review or revisit a triage decision later.

questions.competency: VII.B — Foundational Operations Concepts, Resource Protection, and Incident Management
questions.skill: Assessing breach notification exposure after loss of an encrypted removable device
questions.performanceIndicator: Weigh encryption status and control effectiveness when determining incident handling and reporting obligations
questions.scenarioContext: A pharmacy chain's field auditor reports that a company-issued removable drive containing patient prescription records is missing after a site visit. The drive was provisioned with full-disk encryption, and the encryption key was never stored with the device.
questions.prompt: How should the security team approach this event?

choices.A: Treat it identically to loss of unencrypted data, since any missing device is automatically reportable regardless of controls
choices.B: Assume no risk exists and close the matter without further review because the drive was encrypted
choices.C: Investigate the encryption configuration and key management, then determine reporting obligations based on the confirmed control effectiveness
choices.D: Wait to see whether the data appears publicly before taking any action

questions.explanation: The appropriate response confirms whether the encryption was properly configured and the key remained protected, since verified strong encryption can materially reduce or eliminate breach notification obligations depending on applicable requirements. Treating every loss identically ignores the risk-reducing effect of verified encryption. Assuming safety without verification is premature, and waiting for public exposure abandons timely incident handling.

questions.competency: VII.C — Detection, Prevention, Patch, and Change Management
questions.skill: Conducting periodic firewall rule-base review to remove stale or overly permissive rules
questions.performanceIndicator: Maintain a firewall rule base that reflects current, justified business need
questions.scenarioContext: An aerospace parts manufacturer's firewall rule base has grown over several years with rules added for projects that have since ended. A recent review finds multiple broad rules with no documented owner or current business justification.
questions.prompt: What should the security team do with the unjustified broad rules?

choices.A: Leave the rules in place in case a project resumes at an undetermined future date
choices.B: Validate current business need with rule owners, then remove or narrow rules that are no longer justified
choices.C: Widen the rules further so future projects will not require new firewall requests
choices.D: Disable the entire firewall rule base and rebuild it during the next scheduled outage window

questions.explanation: Validating current need with accountable owners and then removing or narrowing unjustified rules keeps the rule base aligned with actual business requirements and reduces unnecessary exposure. Leaving speculative rules in place preserves avoidable risk. Widening rules further increases exposure, and disabling the entire rule base is disruptive and unnecessary when a targeted review can address the specific stale entries.

questions.competency: VII.C — Detection, Prevention, Patch, and Change Management
questions.skill: Responding when malware evades signature-based anti-malware detection
questions.performanceIndicator: Use behavioral detection and endpoint response capabilities when signature-based tools fail to identify a threat
questions.scenarioContext: An online gaming platform's signature-based anti-malware tool did not flag a workstation later found to be communicating with a known malicious infrastructure address. Endpoint detection and response tooling is available but not yet configured for this workstation class.
questions.prompt: What is the BEST way to address this detection gap?

choices.A: Rely solely on periodic signature updates and wait for vendor coverage to improve
choices.B: Extend behavioral endpoint detection and response coverage to this workstation class and investigate the affected host
choices.C: Remove anti-malware tooling from this workstation class since it did not detect the activity
choices.D: Disable outbound network access for all workstations of this class indefinitely

questions.explanation: Extending behavioral endpoint detection and response coverage addresses threats that signature-based tools miss, while investigating the affected host determines the scope of this specific compromise. Waiting on signature updates alone leaves the same detection gap unaddressed. Removing the existing tool eliminates a layer that still has value, and an indefinite blanket network restriction is disproportionate to a targeted detection gap.

questions.competency: VII.C — Detection, Prevention, Patch, and Change Management
questions.skill: Applying staged patch testing before production deployment
questions.performanceIndicator: Validate patch compatibility and stability before applying updates broadly
questions.scenarioContext: A pediatric specialty clinic network's IT team receives a routine vendor security patch for its electronic health record application. The patch has not yet been evaluated against the clinic's specific configuration.
questions.prompt: What should the team do BEFORE deploying the patch to all production systems?

choices.A: Apply the patch to all systems simultaneously to close the vulnerability as quickly as possible
choices.B: Test the patch in a representative non-production environment and confirm compatibility before broader deployment
choices.C: Skip testing because the vendor has already validated the patch internally
choices.D: Delay the patch indefinitely until the next major version upgrade

questions.explanation: Testing the patch in a representative non-production environment confirms compatibility with the clinic's specific configuration before it reaches every production system, reducing the risk of unexpected disruption. Deploying everywhere at once skips that verification. Vendor testing does not account for site-specific configurations, and indefinite delay leaves a known vulnerability unaddressed longer than necessary.

questions.competency: VII.C — Detection, Prevention, Patch, and Change Management
questions.skill: Recognizing when a change qualifies for a pre-approved standard change process
questions.performanceIndicator: Distinguish low-risk, repeatable changes from those requiring full change advisory board review
questions.scenarioContext: A public library system's change management program allows certain well-understood, low-risk, repeatable changes to follow a lighter pre-approved process rather than full change advisory board review. IT staff are unsure whether a routine, previously validated configuration update qualifies.
questions.prompt: Which characteristic BEST qualifies a change for the pre-approved standard change process?

choices.A: The change is well understood, low risk, follows a documented and previously validated procedure, and has a known rollback method
choices.B: The change has never been performed before but appears simple to implement
choices.C: The change affects a critical system, so expedited handling is appropriate regardless of documentation
choices.D: The requester is confident the change will not cause any problems

questions.explanation: A pre-approved standard change is one that is well understood, low risk, follows a documented and previously validated procedure, and has a known way to reverse it if needed. An unperformed change lacks the track record standard classification requires. Criticality alone does not justify skipping appropriate review, and a requester's confidence is not a substitute for documented, validated criteria.

questions.competency: VII.D — Recovery Strategies and Disaster Recovery Processes
questions.skill: Selecting a hot site to meet a near-immediate recovery time objective
questions.performanceIndicator: Match recovery-site readiness to a stringent but not zero-downtime recovery requirement
questions.scenarioContext: A national parcel shipping company must restore its package-routing system within a small number of minutes after losing its primary data center. The organization can accept installing and starting pre-configured, ready standby equipment but cannot tolerate the cost of continuously mirrored, real-time synchronized processing.
questions.prompt: Which recovery site BEST fits this requirement?

choices.A: A cold site with space and utilities but no installed processing equipment
choices.B: A warm site requiring several hours of configuration and data restoration
choices.C: A hot site with installed, largely configured systems that can be brought into service within minutes
choices.D: A mirrored site with continuous real-time synchronization and immediate failover

questions.explanation: A hot site provides installed, largely configured systems that can be activated within minutes, meeting a stringent recovery time objective without the continuous synchronization cost of a mirrored site. A cold site requires far more time to become operational. A warm site's multi-hour restoration window does not meet a near-immediate requirement, and a mirrored site exceeds both the stated need and the accepted budget.

questions.competency: VII.D — Recovery Strategies and Disaster Recovery Processes
questions.skill: Selecting a backup type and rotation scheme to fit a defined backup window and storage constraint
questions.performanceIndicator: Balance backup duration, storage consumption, and restoration complexity against operational constraints
questions.scenarioContext: An agricultural cooperative's nightly backup window has become too short for a full backup of its growing inventory and shipment database, and available backup storage is limited. Management wants backups to complete reliably within the window without exceeding storage capacity.
questions.prompt: Which approach would BEST address the described constraint?

choices.A: Continue full backups every night regardless of the time and storage required
choices.B: Combine periodic full backups with more frequent incremental or differential backups between them
choices.C: Stop backing up the database until additional storage budget is approved
choices.D: Back up the database only once a month to reduce storage consumption

questions.explanation: Combining periodic full backups with more frequent incremental or differential backups reduces the time and storage each nightly job requires while still supporting restoration to a recent point. Continuing nightly full backups preserves the same window and storage pressure. Suspending backups leaves data unprotected, and monthly-only backups would allow far more data loss than the organization likely intends.

questions.competency: VII.D — Recovery Strategies and Disaster Recovery Processes
questions.skill: Improving high availability of an application tier through load-balanced clustering
questions.performanceIndicator: Eliminate a single point of failure in a service tier through redundant, load-balanced design
questions.scenarioContext: An online brokerage platform currently runs its order-entry application on a single server. A hardware or software failure on that server currently takes the entire order-entry function offline until a replacement is brought up manually.
questions.prompt: How should the platform improve the availability of the order-entry function?

choices.A: Deploy the application across a load-balanced cluster of servers so a single failure does not remove the service
choices.B: Increase the memory allocated to the existing single server
choices.C: Move the application to a different single server with newer hardware
choices.D: Schedule more frequent manual health checks on the existing server

questions.explanation: A load-balanced cluster removes the single point of failure by distributing the order-entry function across multiple servers, so one failure does not take the service offline. Adding memory or moving to newer hardware still leaves a single point of failure. More frequent manual health checks can shorten detection time but do not prevent an outage when the sole server fails.

questions.competency: VII.D — Recovery Strategies and Disaster Recovery Processes
questions.skill: Recognizing the characteristics of a read-through disaster recovery test
questions.performanceIndicator: Distinguish a checklist-style individual plan review from group-based or system-activating test types
questions.scenarioContext: A regional airport authority is conducting the first review of a newly drafted disaster recovery plan. Each plan owner is asked to individually read their assigned sections and confirm they are accurate and current, without any group discussion or system activity.
questions.prompt: Which TWO characteristics describe this type of disaster recovery test? Select 2 of the 5 options below.

choices.A: Each plan owner independently reviews their assigned sections for accuracy and currency
choices.B: Cross-functional teams gather to discuss the plan and talk through a sample scenario together
choices.C: No recovery systems or production services are activated at any point during the review
choices.D: Recovered systems operate in parallel with production so results can be compared
choices.E: Completing this review alone satisfies the organization's requirement for a full interruption test

questions.explanation: A read-through test involves individual review of the plan for accuracy and currency, with no systems activated and no group exercise conducted. Group discussion of a sample scenario describes a walkthrough rather than a read-through. Parallel operation of recovered systems describes a different, more advanced test type, and an individual read-through does not substitute for the operational assurance a full interruption test provides.

questions.competency: VII.E — Business Continuity Planning, Physical Security, and Personnel Safety
questions.skill: Conducting a Business Impact Analysis to identify critical processes and recovery priorities
questions.performanceIndicator: Establish recovery priorities and objectives from documented business impact rather than assumption
questions.scenarioContext: A ride-sharing company is beginning formal business continuity planning for the first time. Leadership has drafted a recovery strategy based on which systems the technology team believes are most important, without input from the business units that depend on them.
questions.prompt: What should the organization do BEFORE finalizing recovery priorities?

choices.A: Conduct a business impact analysis with business units to identify critical processes, dependencies, and recovery objectives
choices.B: Finalize the plan as drafted since the technology team understands the systems best
choices.C: Set identical recovery time objectives for every system to avoid the analysis effort
choices.D: Wait until after the next actual disruption to learn which systems matter most

questions.explanation: A business impact analysis conducted with the business units that depend on each process produces defensible, evidence-based recovery priorities and objectives, rather than assumptions made by the technology team alone. Finalizing the draft without that input risks misaligned priorities. Treating every system as equally critical ignores real differences in impact, and waiting for an actual disruption forfeits the chance to plan proactively.

questions.competency: VII.E — Business Continuity Planning, Physical Security, and Personnel Safety
questions.skill: Selecting appropriate fire suppression for a data center equipment room
questions.performanceIndicator: Balance equipment protection and personnel life safety when choosing a suppression system for a sensitive environment
questions.scenarioContext: A colocation data center provider is finalizing fire protection for a new equipment room housing customer servers and storage arrays. Water-based suppression could protect the building structure but risks damaging the electronic equipment it is meant to save.
questions.prompt: Which approach BEST balances equipment protection and personnel safety in this environment?

choices.A: Install a clean-agent suppression system suited to electronic equipment, supported by appropriate detection and evacuation procedures
choices.B: Rely on a standard water sprinkler system because it is the least expensive option
choices.C: Install no fire suppression system to avoid any risk of equipment damage
choices.D: Use a suppression agent chosen without regard to occupant safety during discharge

questions.explanation: A clean-agent suppression system is designed to control fire in equipment-dense environments while limiting damage to electronics, and pairing it with proper detection and evacuation procedures addresses personnel safety. Standard water sprinklers risk significant equipment damage. Omitting suppression entirely leaves both life safety and equipment at risk, and selecting an agent without regard to occupant safety during discharge disregards a core requirement of the decision.

questions.competency: VII.E — Business Continuity Planning, Physical Security, and Personnel Safety
questions.skill: Implementing a mass notification system for emergency communication to distributed personnel
questions.performanceIndicator: Select a communication method that reliably reaches personnel across multiple locations during an emergency
questions.scenarioContext: A large K-12 school district currently relies on individual office staff making phone calls to notify each school during an emergency. A recent drill showed that some schools received notification many minutes after others, delaying protective actions.
questions.prompt: What should the district implement to improve emergency communication?

choices.A: A mass notification system that can reach all schools simultaneously through multiple channels
choices.B: A requirement that only the superintendent's office may originate any emergency call
choices.C: A single shared phone line that each school must call in sequence to receive updates
choices.D: A policy directing schools to wait for a printed bulletin before taking protective action

questions.explanation: A mass notification system that reaches all schools simultaneously through multiple channels closes the timing gap that sequential manual calling creates. Centralizing origination in one office does not by itself solve the delay in reaching recipients. A single shared line that each school must call in sequence recreates the same delay, and waiting for a printed bulletin is far too slow for protective action during an emergency.

questions.competency: VIII.A — Security in the Software Development Life Cycle
questions.skill: Tailoring security activities to different development methodologies
questions.performanceIndicator: Preserve common security objectives while adapting control timing and evidence to each delivery model
questions.scenarioContext: After an acquisition, a telecommunications company has one team using a phase-gated Waterfall process and another releasing through short Agile iterations. Leadership wants a single secure development policy without forcing both teams into the same workflow.
questions.prompt: Which approach would BEST meet this objective?

choices.A: Require both teams to use identical security documents and approval dates regardless of their delivery method.
choices.B: Let each team define its own security objectives because methodology determines acceptable risk.
choices.C: Define common security outcomes and required evidence, then map activities and decision points to each methodology's lifecycle.
choices.D: Apply security requirements only to the Waterfall team because iterative development cannot support formal assurance.

questions.explanation: Common security outcomes establish consistent expectations, while methodology-specific mappings place reviews, testing, and evidence where they work in each lifecycle. Identical schedules can disrupt delivery without improving assurance. Teams should not independently redefine risk objectives, and iterative development can support formal controls through recurring, automated, and risk-based activities.

questions.competency: VIII.A — Security in the Software Development Life Cycle
questions.skill: Establishing an effective software security champion program
questions.performanceIndicator: Distribute security expertise while preserving central governance and escalation
questions.scenarioContext: A multinational retailer has too few application security specialists to attend every development meeting. Engineering leaders propose naming a security champion within each product team.
questions.prompt: What is the MOST important condition for the program to succeed?

choices.A: Provide champions with defined responsibilities, training, protected time, central guidance, and an escalation path to security specialists.
choices.B: Transfer full risk acceptance authority to champions so central security review is no longer required.
choices.C: Select only the most senior developer on each team, regardless of interest or available time.
choices.D: Measure the program solely by the number of security messages champions send to their teams.

questions.explanation: Champions need clear duties, competence, time, support, and escalation so they can embed security without becoming isolated substitutes for specialists or management. Risk acceptance remains with authorized management. Seniority alone does not ensure engagement or capacity, and message volume does not demonstrate improved software outcomes.

questions.competency: VIII.A — Security in the Software Development Life Cycle
questions.skill: Governing security in outsourced software development
questions.performanceIndicator: Retain accountability through contractual requirements, evidence, and acceptance controls
questions.scenarioContext: A regional bank will hire an external firm to build a customer onboarding application. The business sponsor assumes the supplier's standard development process will transfer responsibility for software security to the supplier.
questions.prompt: What should the security manager recommend FIRST?

choices.A: Accept the supplier's process without review because contractual outsourcing transfers security accountability.
choices.B: Wait until final delivery and use a penetration test as the only software security acceptance criterion.
choices.C: Give the supplier unrestricted access to production data so functional testing matches real operations.
choices.D: Define security requirements, development practices, evidence, defect remediation, data handling, and acceptance rights in the agreement and governance plan.

questions.explanation: The bank retains accountability and should establish enforceable expectations, evidence, remediation duties, data controls, and acceptance criteria before development begins. Outsourcing work does not outsource risk ownership. A final penetration test is useful but too narrow as the sole control, and unrestricted production data creates unnecessary exposure.

questions.competency: VIII.A — Security in the Software Development Life Cycle
questions.skill: Selecting meaningful secure development performance metrics
questions.performanceIndicator: Measure risk reduction and process effectiveness rather than raw activity volume
questions.scenarioContext: A software director wants metrics that show whether secure development practices are reducing material risk across several product teams. Current reports show only the total number of scanner findings generated each month.
questions.prompt: Which TWO metrics would provide the MOST useful improvement evidence? Select 2 of the 5 options below.

choices.A: The raw number of findings produced by every tool without validation or normalization.
choices.B: The rate and severity of vulnerabilities escaping to later lifecycle stages or production, normalized to meaningful delivery units.
choices.C: The number of source-code lines added by each team during the reporting period.
choices.D: The percentage of developers who opened the annual training invitation email.
choices.E: Risk-tiered remediation time and recurrence trends for validated vulnerability classes.

questions.explanation: Escaped-vulnerability trends show whether controls detect problems early, while risk-tiered remediation and recurrence reveal responsiveness and whether root causes are being addressed. Raw tool output is distorted by false positives and scan coverage. Code volume is not a risk measure, and opening a training invitation does not demonstrate learning or improved behavior.

questions.competency: VIII.A — Security in the Software Development Life Cycle
questions.skill: Separating development and test environments from production
questions.performanceIndicator: Protect production data and credentials while enabling representative nonproduction testing
questions.scenarioContext: A mortgage company lets developers troubleshoot in a test environment that shares production service credentials and receives nightly copies of unmasked customer data. The team says this arrangement is necessary to reproduce defects accurately.
questions.prompt: Which remediation BEST balances testing needs with lifecycle security?

choices.A: Keep the shared credentials but rotate them whenever a developer leaves the company.
choices.B: Segregate the environments, issue separate least-privilege credentials, and use masked, minimized, or synthetic test data with controlled exceptions.
choices.C: Continue copying production data but require developers to acknowledge its sensitivity each month.
choices.D: Eliminate the test environment and require all defect reproduction to occur in production under supervision.

questions.explanation: Environment separation, distinct credentials, and safe representative data reduce the chance that development activity compromises production or exposes customers. Rotation on departure does not correct shared privilege. Acknowledgment is not a data protection control, and production troubleshooting increases operational and security risk rather than containing it.

questions.competency: VIII.B — Security Controls in Development Ecosystems and Secure Coding
questions.skill: Preventing operating system command injection
questions.performanceIndicator: Separate untrusted input from command interpretation and constrain permitted operations
questions.scenarioContext: A media conversion service constructs a shell command by concatenating a user-supplied output filename. Character filtering is applied, but reviewers demonstrate several encoding techniques that still alter the command.
questions.prompt: What is the BEST corrective action?

choices.A: Replace shell invocation with a safe library interface that passes validated allow-listed values as distinct arguments under least privilege.
choices.B: Expand the deny list whenever a new command separator is discovered during testing.
choices.C: Run the existing shell command with additional logging so suspicious filenames can be investigated.
choices.D: Encode the completed command before execution and decode it inside the shell process.

questions.explanation: Avoiding the shell removes command interpretation from the data path, while allow-listed arguments and least privilege provide additional protection. A deny list is difficult to make complete across encodings and shell behavior. Logging is detective, and encoding the same command does not prevent the shell from interpreting malicious content after decoding.

questions.competency: VIII.B — Security Controls in Development Ecosystems and Secure Coding
questions.skill: Eliminating a time-of-check to time-of-use race condition
questions.performanceIndicator: Use atomic operations and trusted handles instead of separately checking and reopening a resource
questions.scenarioContext: A print service verifies that a temporary file belongs to the requesting user, closes it, and later reopens the same path for processing. An attacker can replace the path between the ownership check and the reopen operation.
questions.prompt: Which design change MOST directly addresses the vulnerability?

choices.A: Repeat the ownership check once per hour and retain the existing open sequence.
choices.B: Choose longer temporary filenames so an attacker is less likely to predict the path.
choices.C: Log the path before and after processing to support investigation of replaced files.
choices.D: Open and validate the resource through an atomic, secure operation and continue using the validated handle rather than reopening by path.

questions.explanation: An atomic secure open and continued use of the validated handle remove the gap in which the path can be redirected between check and use. Periodic checking does not protect an individual operation. Less predictable names can help but do not eliminate the race, and logging detects evidence after the unsafe access may have occurred.

questions.competency: VIII.B — Security Controls in Development Ecosystems and Secure Coding
questions.skill: Preventing cross-site request forgery in state-changing requests
questions.performanceIndicator: Require proof that sensitive browser requests originated from the intended application context
questions.scenarioContext: A payroll portal uses session cookies and accepts a state-changing request that updates direct-deposit details. A user who is logged in can be induced by another website to submit the request without realizing it.
questions.prompt: Which control is the BEST primary defense?

choices.A: Increase the session cookie length while leaving the request workflow unchanged.
choices.B: Hide the direct-deposit form URL from users who have not recently visited the payroll home page.
choices.C: Require a validated anti-forgery token for state-changing requests and use appropriate cookie protections as defense in depth.
choices.D: Encrypt the employee database so forged requests cannot modify stored account information.

questions.explanation: An unpredictable request-bound anti-forgery token demonstrates that the action originated through the legitimate application flow; suitable SameSite and other cookie settings add defense in depth. Cookie length protects against guessing, not cross-site submission. Hidden URLs do not enforce origin, and database encryption does not stop the authenticated application from processing a forged request.

questions.competency: VIII.B — Security Controls in Development Ecosystems and Secure Coding
questions.skill: Governing container base images in the development ecosystem
questions.performanceIndicator: Maintain trusted, minimal, current, and traceable runtime foundations
questions.scenarioContext: A scientific computing company allows project teams to select arbitrary public container base images. Scans show inconsistent operating system packages, outdated components, and images whose maintainers cannot be identified.
questions.prompt: Which program would BEST reduce this recurring risk?

choices.A: Permit any public image if the project team records its download date in the repository.
choices.B: Provide approved minimal base images from a controlled registry, verify provenance, scan and rebuild them regularly, and track dependent applications.
choices.C: Scan finished application code while excluding base image packages from the component inventory.
choices.D: Allow teams to retain outdated images when the container starts successfully in a development environment.

questions.explanation: Controlled minimal images with verified provenance, recurring maintenance, and dependency tracking reduce unknown components and make affected applications identifiable when an image changes. A download date does not establish trust. Application-only scanning misses operating system packages, and successful startup provides no evidence that an old image is secure.

questions.competency: VIII.B — Security Controls in Development Ecosystems and Secure Coding
questions.skill: Preventing sensitive data exposure through application logs
questions.performanceIndicator: Design logging that supports operations without recording unnecessary secrets or personal data
questions.scenarioContext: A telehealth application records complete request bodies to help support staff diagnose errors. The logs now contain authentication tokens and patient details, and they are retained in a broadly accessible analytics platform.
questions.prompt: What is the BEST remediation strategy?

choices.A: Encrypt the existing logs but continue collecting complete request bodies for every transaction.
choices.B: Obtain user consent for diagnostic logging and leave access and retention unchanged.
choices.C: Move the same logs to a separate storage account while preserving broad support access.
choices.D: Define an allow-listed logging schema, redact or exclude sensitive fields, restrict access, set risk-based retention, and test logging behavior.

questions.explanation: Data minimization at the source prevents unnecessary secrets and health information from entering logs, while access, retention, and testing provide layered protection. Encryption does not justify excessive collection. Consent alone does not correct insecure design, and moving the data without reducing content or access preserves the underlying exposure.

questions.competency: VIII.C — Assessing Software Security and Acquired Software Risk
questions.skill: Improving static analysis signal quality and governance
questions.performanceIndicator: Tune automated findings without hiding accepted or unresolved risk
questions.scenarioContext: A tax preparation software team receives thousands of static analysis alerts. Developers have begun ignoring the reports because many findings are not exploitable in the application's context, yet some high-risk defects have also been missed during triage.
questions.prompt: What should the application security manager do?

choices.A: Validate representative findings, tune rules using contextual evidence, prioritize by risk, and govern suppressions with owners, rationale, and review dates.
choices.B: Disable static analysis until the tool can produce a report with no false positives.
choices.C: Require developers to remediate every alert in the order generated, regardless of exploitability or severity.
choices.D: Automatically suppress any rule that generated more findings than the team closed during the previous release.

questions.explanation: Evidence-based tuning and risk prioritization improve signal quality, while governed suppressions preserve accountability for accepted or context-dependent findings. Eliminating the technique forfeits early detection. Treating every alert equally wastes effort, and volume-based suppression can conceal important weaknesses without considering exploitability or impact.

questions.competency: VIII.C — Assessing Software Security and Acquired Software Risk
questions.skill: Expanding authenticated application security test coverage
questions.performanceIndicator: Align runtime testing with roles, states, workflows, and application inventory
questions.scenarioContext: A university scans its student services application dynamically without authentication. The scan reports few findings, but most functions are available only after login and behavior differs among student, instructor, and administrator roles.
questions.prompt: Which change would MOST improve the assessment's coverage?

choices.A: Increase the unauthenticated scan rate so the public login page receives more requests.
choices.B: Treat the small finding count as evidence that protected functions are secure.
choices.C: Provide controlled test identities for relevant roles, map authenticated workflows and states, and supplement runtime testing where coverage gaps remain.
choices.D: Disable role separation in the test environment so one account can access every function.

questions.explanation: Role-specific test identities and mapped workflows allow runtime assessment of the functions, authorization paths, and application states users actually reach. Faster requests to the public surface do not add authenticated coverage. A low finding count may reflect limited reach, and removing role separation changes the behavior that must be assessed.

questions.competency: VIII.C — Assessing Software Security and Acquired Software Risk
questions.skill: Assessing data risk from a third-party mobile software development kit
questions.performanceIndicator: Evaluate component behavior, permissions, data flows, and supplier obligations before integration
questions.scenarioContext: A fitness application team wants to add a third-party analytics software development kit. The package requests device identifiers and location permissions that exceed the team's stated measurement needs, and its data destinations are not fully documented.
questions.prompt: What should the security and privacy reviewers recommend FIRST?

choices.A: Integrate the package because mobile operating system permissions provide sufficient supplier assurance.
choices.B: Map and test the SDK's data collection and destinations, challenge unnecessary permissions, assess the supplier, and establish enforceable data-handling terms before approval.
choices.C: Publish a broad privacy notice after release without changing the SDK configuration or integration decision.
choices.D: Allow the SDK to collect all requested data and delete the application's local copy immediately afterward.

questions.explanation: Reviewers need evidence about actual data flows, necessity, supplier controls, and enforceable obligations before embedding third-party code. Operating system permissions expose capabilities but do not prove appropriate use. Notice alone does not minimize collection, and deleting a local copy does not control data already transmitted to the supplier.

questions.competency: VIII.C — Assessing Software Security and Acquired Software Risk
questions.skill: Retiring an insecure legacy API version
questions.performanceIndicator: Reduce persistent application exposure through governed API lifecycle management
questions.scenarioContext: An online marketplace has released a new API version with stronger validation and authorization controls. Several partners still use the older version, which remains internet-accessible and cannot support the new controls.
questions.prompt: What is the BEST risk treatment?

choices.A: Keep both versions available indefinitely because partner compatibility has priority over control consistency.
choices.B: Hide the older version from public documentation while continuing to accept requests to it.
choices.C: Apply the new controls only at the client side for partners that cannot migrate.
choices.D: Inventory consumers, communicate a supported migration path and deadline, monitor adoption, apply interim restrictions, and decommission the legacy version.

questions.explanation: A governed deprecation process balances partner transition with a defined end to the insecure exposure, using visibility and interim safeguards while migration occurs. Indefinite support preserves the weakness. Removing documentation is obscurity, and client-side controls cannot reliably compensate for missing server-side validation and authorization.

questions.competency: VIII.C — Assessing Software Security and Acquired Software Risk
questions.skill: Designing source-code escrow for critical acquired software
questions.performanceIndicator: Ensure escrow materials are current, releasable, and usable when defined supplier failures occur
questions.scenarioContext: A food processing company depends on proprietary software from a small supplier for plant scheduling. Replacement would take many months, and executives are concerned that supplier failure could leave the company without security updates or maintenance capability.
questions.prompt: Which TWO provisions would make source-code escrow MOST effective? Select 2 of the 5 options below.

choices.A: Define objective release triggers and require current source, dependencies, build instructions, and necessary documentation to be deposited on a recurring basis.
choices.B: Store only the original installation binary because compiled software is sufficient for future maintenance.
choices.C: Allow the supplier to decide after a business failure whether the customer qualifies to receive the deposit.
choices.D: Treat the existence of an escrow agreement as proof that deposited materials can produce a maintainable application.
choices.E: Arrange independent periodic verification that deposits are complete, retrievable, and capable of producing the agreed software.

questions.explanation: Objective triggers and recurring complete deposits establish when and what can be released, while independent verification demonstrates that the materials are usable rather than merely present. A binary alone does not enable source maintenance. Supplier discretion can defeat access when the supplier is unavailable, and an untested agreement does not prove buildability or completeness.
